newsitem.title: UK: Argos leads UK retailers down on rate fears.
newsitem.headline: Argos leads UK retailers down on rate fears.

text.p: Argos Plc led UK UK retailing stocks lower on Tuesday amid renewed fears that higher domestic interest rates could choke off the recent recovery in consumer spending, dealers said.

By 1217 GMT, Argos was down 18p, or 2.4 percent, at 733, Great Universal Stores Plc was eight pence weaker at 613 and Marks and Spencer Plc had eased five pence to 482. Dixons Group Plc dropped seven pence to 536-1/2.
"There's no specific story behind it but the market's been worried about interest rates and retailers have been hit more than most by this," one market-maker said.
"People are worried higher interest rates will halt their recovery in its tracks this year," he said.

Dixons reports half-year results on Wednesday and Argos makes its Christmas trading statement on Friday, but dealers said the figures were expected to be relatively strong and unlikely to upset the market.

"There's maybe some nervousness about the Dixons figures and Argos statement but I would have thought they'd be reasonably bullish," another market-maker said. "So unless someone thinks they have an inside track on the figures, I don't think they're behind the weakness today," he said.

Fears of a near-term rise in British interest rates have been haunting London shares for some time, but received new fuel from Monday's UK M0 money supply figures which showed a sharper-than-expected rise in December.
